provenance.notes: Int family batch. Small tickets, so every add-on and product is priced low; copy leans on the to-do list, minimum visits and what a handyman can't legally do. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Upload a list of small home jobs with a photo each, half-day and full-day visit blocks, the minimum visit, and what typically fits into one handyman trip
pageStructurePlus.why: Handyman customers don't have one job, they have a list. Booking around the list is how a two-hour call becomes a full day.

pageStructurePlus.section: What a handyman does, and what gets referred out
pageStructurePlus.contains: Small repairs, patching, doors and trim, fixtures and caulking, versus panel work, gas lines and major plumbing that need a licensed trade, and who they recommend for those
pageStructurePlus.why: People worry about hiring a handyman for something that needs a licence. Being clear about limits builds trust and keeps them legal.

pageStructurePlus.contains: TV mounting on drywall, plaster and brick, floating shelves, curtain rods, mirrors and art, flat-pack furniture assembly and the right anchors for each wall
pageStructurePlus.why: Mounting and assembly are the most searched handyman jobs and the easiest first booking. A page per task catches those searches.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Grab bars into studs, stair railings, smoke and carbon monoxide detector swaps, lever door handles, brighter stair lighting and non-slip treads
pageStructurePlus.why: Adult children book these for parents and search by the worry. A calm page with a clear visit price wins that call.

pageStructurePlus.section: Small-repair punch lists for landlords and agents
pageStructurePlus.contains: Move-out repair lists, inspection repair items before closing, completion photos for the manager, keys and lockbox access, and invoices that go straight to the owner
pageStructurePlus.why: Repeat landlord and agent work is what fills a handyman's slow weeks. These buyers decide on speed and paperwork, not price.

designDirections.name: Tool Belt
designDirections.bestFor: Solo handymen who win on answering the phone and showing up when they said they would
designDirections.headlineSample: Handyman repairs around the home in {City}, booked fast
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a plain grotesque read like a work order. Tap-to-call and the to-do list form are the only two things on the first screen.

designDirections.name: Book a Visit
designDirections.bestFor: Handyman services selling half-day and full-day blocks that customers can book and fill with a list
designDirections.headlineSample: Book a handyman visit for your to-do list in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Butter and Denim passes, and its friendly geometric type suits a booking-first site where cards list visit lengths and tasks.

designDirections.name: Trusted at Home
designDirections.bestFor: Established handyman firms serving older homeowners, landlords and agents who care most about trust
designDirections.headlineSample: A handyman you can trust in your home, across {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Evergreen and a refined serif feel like a family insurer, which is what an older homeowner letting someone in wants to feel.

openers.line: Anyone in {City} searching 'handyman near me' sees your rating on Maps, then nothing to tap but a phone number. A website would show them the small jobs you take.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a handyman customer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing's link opens a Facebook page. A homeowner with a list of six small repairs wants to know your minimum visit and whether you mount TVs, not scroll a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the most recent job they posted.
openers.linkLine: A handyman page that answers the to-do list question: {demo-link}

openers.line: The handyman site on your listing still has a free-host banner and the services list stops at 'and more'. People booking a stranger into their home read that closely.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, old copyright or vague service list. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Your handyman business, current and clear: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site's call button sits under the menu on my phone. Handyman calls are made on the spot, standing next to the dripping faucet or the door that won't latch.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same handyman site, fixed for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most handyman calls start with 'I have a few things'. A form where people type the list and add a photo of each job would let you price the visit before you drive over.
openers.hook: Check for any form. If booking is only by call or text, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A to-do list form for handyman visits: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Small jobs, nowhere to show them
openers.line: The shelving wall and the rebuilt gate you posted show you're tidy with small home repairs. Grouped by task, those posts would book the next mounting or door job.
openers.hook: Find two small jobs on their page you can name by task. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your handyman jobs sorted by task: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say you showed up on time and fixed three things nobody else would bother with. That's exactly what a handyman customer is searching for, and it's buried on Maps.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about punctuality or small jobs. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the handyman work: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring and autumn are when every homeowner writes the list: gutters, screens, caulk, sticking doors. The handyman they find that week gets the whole list.
openers.hook: Use this March to April or September to October. Name the season in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A handyman page ready for the seasonal list: {demo-link}

openers.line: People notice the loose railing at nine at night. If they can book a handyman visit right then, they don't search again in the morning.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it's voicemail only and there's no booking, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A handyman booking that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a second handyman. Someone handy and reliable will check your business out online before they call, and a real site helps them say yes.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A handyman site with a page for new hires: {demo-link}

openers.line: You do handyman work across {City}, but someone in {Neighborhood} can't tell if you'll drive out for a two-hour job. A page per area answers that.
openers.hook: Find areas mentioned in reviews. Use the one furthest from them.
openers.linkLine: A handyman page for each area you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first thing anyone asks a handyman is the minimum charge. If you have a set visit rate, a page saying it saves you answering that call over and over.
openers.hook: Only if they've ever posted a rate or visit minimum. Otherwise lead with the to-do list angle.
openers.linkLine: Handyman visit pricing explained up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: Letting someone into the house for a small home repair is a bigger decision than the job itself. A page with your insurance and who'll actually show up settles that.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance anywhere. Note it if they do; never invent it.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and who shows up, on one handyman page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your handyman calendar fills from neighbours and repeat customers. That's great until a few move away, and even a neighbour's referral looks you up first.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'neighbour recommended' or 'use him for everything'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a handyman referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is careful handyman work. A small job done that neatly is what convinces a stranger to call.
openers.hook: Pick their newest posted job and name the task exactly.
openers.linkLine: That handyman job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is tidy handyman work.

I was looking for handyman services in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no site where someone can send their to-do list or see what you take on. I put together a sample handyman site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want to see it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample handyman site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a to-do list form with a photo per job, a clear page on what you do and refer out, and visit blocks people can book. If it's not for you, say the word.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for handyman businesses here in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample handyman site for {Business Name}, with a to-do list form, visit blocks and a page on what you do and don't do, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many task and area pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a handyman business your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, and the to-do list form is built to turn short calls into full-day visits."
"Can I show you around it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. If you'd rather split it in two payments, that's fine."

objections.objection: My jobs are too small to pay for a website.
objections.handler: "That's the point of the to-do list form. People send six small jobs at once, and a two-hour call becomes a full day. One extra full day a month covers the care plan."

objections.objection: I'm already booked solid with regulars.
objections.handler: "Then the site filters. Visit minimums and the list form keep the one-hinge calls away and let you choose the full days."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead platform for handyman jobs.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several handymen and you pay either way. Your own site sends that homeowner and their whole list to one handyman, you."

objections.objection: I don't want to publish prices, every job's different.
objections.handler: "Fair. We publish the visit minimum and the half-day block, not job prices. That's the number people ask before anything else."
"You won't touch it. The list comes to your phone as a text, and changes are a message to me."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: a to-do list form, a task page set and booking for visit blocks. Two payments if that's easier."

email.subject: Handyman site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for handyman businesses in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link, look when you're between jobs. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} handyman demo down on Friday.

Keep it or let it go? One word is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, it's the time of year when everyone writes their home to-do list. Thought of you.

The handyman site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Keep the build small. Handyman jobs are a few hundred dollars, so price the site against a month of visits, not a single job.
Offer the build in two payments; cash flow matters more than the total for a solo handyman.
The to-do list form with photo per task is the core. Price it inside the build and keep other add-ons cheap.
Task pages (TV mounting, door repair, assembly) are low-cost lines; each catches its own search.
Only quote landlord and agent pages for handymen who already take that work.
Never quote software over a few thousand dollars. A handyman's money is in volume, not in tools.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a photo set, visit length guidance and an FAQ for that task.

lineItems.item: To-do list form with photo per job
lineItems.description: Max with unlimited job rows, photo upload per row, an access-and-parking field and text alerts.
Max with half-day and full-day blocks, travel buffers and a deposit option.
Max with a separate request form, lockbox field and invoice-to-owner option.
Max when each page has its own jobs and a local review.
Max when the task pages and the to-do list form are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for handyman jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week one small handyman job goes on your Google profile, TV mount, door fix or grab bar, so 'handyman near me' shows you working."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review text after each visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Right after you leave, the customer gets a text asking for a review. Handyman reviews pile up fast because the visits are frequent."

whatElseYouSell.name: Fridge magnet and door hanger print run
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A fridge magnet with your number left after every visit, and door hangers on the neighbours' doors. The next home repair call comes from the fridge."

whatElseYouSell.name: Seasonal home maintenance checklist mailer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A spring and autumn home checklist emailed to past customers, with a button to book a handyman visit to tick it off."

whatElseYouSell.name: Nextdoor and neighbourhood group posting kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Neighbourhood groups are where people ask for a handyman. A kit of short posts and before-and-afters makes replying to those threads easy."

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck magnet artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your truck sits in driveways all over town. A clean magnet with the site and 'send me your list' turns that into handyman calls."

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The manager you do repair tickets for needs a simple maintenance request page. Your handyman business is who it sends tickets to."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers have budgets for tenant tools and want reliable small-repair vendors.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents need a vendor page for the inspection repair list before closing, and your handyman name is the first line on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors for a living and pay for pages that make them look organised.

withoutAI.route: Licensed electricians and plumbers they refer to
withoutAI.whoPays: The electrician or plumber, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who do you send the panel and water heater jobs to? I'll build their site, and they'll send small home repairs back to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A natural two-way referral where both sides need a site.

withoutAI.whoPays: The cleaner or organiser, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "House cleaners see the loose towel bar and the broken blind every week. They need a site, and their clients need a handyman's number."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Cleaners are in homes constantly and spot small repairs first.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Care agencies need grab bars and railings installed for clients. A vendor page with a vetted handyman on it is something they'll pay for."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agencies want safe homes and dependable vendors, and the handyman's safety page is the proof.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Rental hosts need fast fixes between guests. A host page with a repair request form routes those jobs to one handyman."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Hosts pay for speed, and repeat repairs between bookings are steady work.

withAI.route: Tenant repair-ticket triage for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenant tickets come in with a photo, get sorted into handyman, plumber or electrician, and the small ones route straight to your client."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers save dispatch time and the handyman gets steady tickets.

withAI.route: Inspection-report repair list extractor for agents
withAI.pitchLine: "Upload the inspection report and get a plain repair list split into handyman items and licensed-trade items, ready to send."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents re-type those lists every closing. A tool that drafts them gets used weekly.

withAI.pitchLine: "When a cleaning client mentions a broken hinge, the assistant offers a handyman visit and books it."
withAI.whyItWorks: The cleaner earns goodwill and the handyman gets the job.

withAI.pitchLine: "Cleaners photograph damage at turnover, the tool writes the repair note and books the handyman before the next guest."
withAI.whyItWorks: Hosts lose bookings to unfixed damage. Fast reporting is worth a small monthly fee.

withAI.pitchLine: "Care managers answer a short questionnaire and get a draft safety-fix list, grab bars and railings, to send to the handyman."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agencies need a record of safety steps, and the handyman does the work.

withAI.pitchLine: "The electrician's site asks callers what they need and sends light-fixture and small home repair jobs to the handyman instead of wasting a truck roll."
withAI.whyItWorks: Electricians want fewer tiny calls; the handyman wants exactly those.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back that asks for the to-do list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Up a ladder when the phone rings? The caller gets a text asking them to send their handyman list with a photo of each job."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Handyman visit price guide by task
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick TV mount, door adjust, grab bar or shelf install and see roughly how much of a handyman visit it takes before booking."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their visit minimum, block rates and typical time per task.

softwareAI.name: Review replies for small home repair jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone thanks you for fixing the sticky slider? A short handyman-style thank-you is drafted for it, and you okay it from the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Same-day invoice with card link
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Finish the handyman visit, tap done, and the invoice with a card link reaches the customer before you've reached the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their payment account and visit rates.

softwareAI.name: To-do list sorter and visit planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A customer's messy list of home repairs comes in, and it drafts the visit length, the parts to bring and anything that needs a licensed trade."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a few months of past lists with actual visit times. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Visit block calendar with travel buffers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers book handyman half-days and full days from your real calendar, with drive time between areas built in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their working hours, areas and block lengths.

softwareAI.name: Evening handyman booking assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening messages, collects the list and photos, flags anything needing a licence, and books a handyman visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar, task list and what they refer out. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Parts list and receipt log per house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every hinge, cartridge and anchor bought for a house logged with the receipt, so materials get billed and nothing's forgotten."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a phone habit of snapping receipts.

softwareAI.name: Home record for repeat customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each house gets a record: paint colours, filter sizes, the faucet model, what was fixed. The next handyman visit starts with answers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their job notes from repeat customers.

softwareAI.name: Repair photo to parts list helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The customer's photo of a leaking faucet or broken latch comes in and it drafts the likely parts to pick up before the handyman visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past jobs with photos and the parts used. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal maintenance reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each spring and autumn, past customers get a home checklist text with a link to book a handyman visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a past customer list and the checklist wording.

softwareAI.name: Landlord ticket board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each landlord sees their open repair tickets, completion photos and invoices on one page, without calling the handyman for updates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for handymen with landlord accounts. Needs their landlord list.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on what the handyman can and can't do
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can you replace an outlet' and 'do you mount TVs on brick' at midnight, from your own rules and limits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their task list and refer-out list, updated as needed. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Membership plan for regular handyman visits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Regulars pay a small monthly amount for a set number of handyman hours a season, booked first and billed automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once they have repeat customers. Needs their hourly rate and how many members they can serve.

softwareAI.name: Weekly earnings by task type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether TV mounting, door work or landlord tickets actually pay best per hour once drive time is counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of visits with times and tasks.

softwareAI.name: Task page writer from job notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month a new handyman task page, like 'mounting a TV over a fireplace', drafted from your notes and approved by you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs short job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to invoice lines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Say what you fixed and the parts on the way out of the house, and it drafts the invoice lines for the handyman visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their rates and invoice format. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Hardware store parts price sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Common parts, anchors, cartridges and hinges, kept at current prices so materials on the handyman invoice are never stale."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their most-used parts list.

softwareAI.name: Booking confirmation and arrival window texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers get a confirmation, a reminder the night before and an on-my-way text, so nobody misses the handyman."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their calendar and wording.

softwareAI.name: Second handyman applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say which home repairs they can do alone, whether they own tools and have a truck, and you only call the real ones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the to-do list form for solo handymen
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The handyman list form with photos per job works for any solo handyman, and there are thousands of them with no site at all."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Huge supply of owner-operators; a cheap monthly tool spreads across many.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Handyman franchisees each need local task pages and their own reviews. One template, rolled out per owner."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Maintenance vendor portal for a property management firm
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every building the firm manages gets one repair request page that routes small jobs to approved handymen."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms buy once and roll out everywhere; small repairs are constant.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A brokerage-wide page for inspection repair lists, with a vetted handyman in each area and a fast turnaround."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokerages want smooth closings and look good offering vetted vendors.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior safety upgrade program with area aging agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The area aging services agency or nonprofit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Aging agencies fund grab bars and railings for seniors. A request portal routes those home safety jobs to vetted handymen."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These programs have budgets and need reliable vendors and records.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Customers at the hardware counter ask who could install what they just bought. A handyman finder on the store's site answers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stores keep pro customers loyal by sending them work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies can't make money building custom sites for a handyman. License my ready handyman template with the list form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Low-ticket clients are only profitable on a template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Co-hosts managing many rentals need one place to send repair requests to local handymen between guests."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Co-hosts manage many units and repairs never stop.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Starter pack for new handyman businesses
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: People starting a handyman business, per pack
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A visit price sheet, a refer-out list template and a one-page handyman site, sold to people going out on their own."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built once, sold many times, and the buyers are numerous.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The home warranty or home services company
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Home warranty claims for minor items need a handyman, not a licensed trade. A dispatch page routes them to vetted locals."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Warranty firms pay to cut costs on minor claims.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A handyman client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One handyman per metro keeps it fair. {City} is taken, so the to-do list template goes to a handyman one metro over."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Quick fixes for broken handyman sites
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The handyman with a dead site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Old handyman sites with dead forms are common. I move them to the list-form template for less than a day's work."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: A cheap, fast fix closes easily with owners who already tried once.

upsellLadder.offer: Visit block calendar with travel buffers

upsellLadder.trigger: They take on a second landlord or property manager account.

upsellLadder.offer: Membership plan for regular handyman visits
upsellLadder.trigger: They have customers who have booked three or more visits.
upsellLadder.line: "Your regulars book every couple of months anyway. A handyman membership makes it steady income."

upsellLadder.trigger: A full season of past customers on file before spring or autumn.
upsellLadder.line: "Every past customer has a spring home list. A reminder sends it to the handyman they already trust."
